subject: Atlas Health — VPC deployment annotated boundaries & handoff
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex@atlashealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Network Ops <netops@atlashealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Atlas Health VPC requirements + initial topology (for review)

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for agreeing to take a look at our private deployment constraints. Attaching a short packet with our current VPC requirements and a rough topology exported from our design tool (atlas-vpc-reqs.pdf). High level asks:

- We need a dedicated VPC with strict control-plane isolation (audit logs forwarded to our SIEM).
- Data-plane (inference nodes) must be in private subnets with no direct internet egress; egress will be via NAT/proxy in a separate security zone.
- KMS-backed key rotation and HSM integration for tenant keys.
- We plan to colocate an edge relay in our primary DC (SFO) and want guidance on routing + failover.

Can your team run a quick architecture review focused on control-plane/data-plane demarcation and provide a minimal annotated diagram and a short ops handoff checklist? Ideally by EOW so we can book a staging cutover in January.

Attachments: atlas-vpc-reqs.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Thanks,
Alex Romero
Dir, Cloud Infrastructure
Atlas Health Systems

Alex — thanks for the packet. We can take this and produce an annotated boundary diagram plus a handoff checklist. Quick clarifying questions before we start the walkthrough:

1) Is the edge relay in SFO expected to host any control-plane components (e.g., webhook endpoints, health-check proxies) or strictly data-plane ingress?
2) Do you have a preferred egress model for outbound dependencies (proxy vs. NAT gateway vs. firewall appliance)?
3) Any hard SLAs for cross-zone latency between control plane and inference nodes?

Plan: Karthik will sketch an initial annotated reference (control-plane/data-plane lanes + recommended CIDR allocations) and I’ll assemble the ops-handoff checklist. Marissa will validate tenant isolation matrix, Kimberly will confirm KMS/HSM constraints.

I’ve attached a lightweight reference template we use for diagrams: vpc-ref-template-v1.pptx — we’ll produce controlplane-dataflow-v2.svg as a first-pass and circulate.

Proposed working session: Tue Dec 22 09:00 PT (30m) — confirm?

Thanks,

On Mon, Dec 20, 2026 at 11:05 AM Irene Choi <irene_ichoi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the packet. We can take this and produce an annotated boundary diagram plus a handoff checklist. Quick clarifying questions before we start the walkthrough:
>
> 1) Is the edge relay in SFO expected to host any control-plane components (e.g., webhook endpoints, health-check proxies) or strictly data-plane ingress?

Alex — answering inline below and adding a first-pass sketch (controlplane-dataflow-v2.svg attached).

Notes / recommendations (first-pass):
- Control plane: keep in a separate management VPC (or a logically isolated management project) with dedicated subnets for API endpoints, telemetry-forwarders, and a bastion for admin access. Control-plane components must be reachable from operator networks only (no public ELB).
- Data plane (inference): private subnets in tenant VPCs. All outbound traffic MUST egress through a tenant-approved proxy cluster in a shared services subnet.
- Edge relay: treat as data-plane ingress only. It should perform request validation and forward to the nearest inference tier; keep webhook callbacks proxied back into the management/control VPC via a secured tunnel (mTLS).

Routing / sample CIDR suggestion (minimal):
- Management/control VPC: 10.10.0.0/16
  - control plane API tier: 10.10.1.0/24
  - telemetry/forwarders: 10.10.2.0/24
- Tenant inference VPC (example tenant-a): 10.40.0.0/16
  - inference private subnets: 10.40.1.0/24 (zone-a), 10.40.2.0/24 (zone-b)
- Shared services (proxy/NAT): 10.60.0.0/24

Firewall / ACL summary:
- Control plane -> Data plane: allow TCP 443 from management subnets to inference nodes for orchestration only; all other control-plane initiated flows must be via an authenticated operator RPC gateway.
- Data plane egress: restricted to proxy cluster. Block direct 0.0.0.0/0 from inference subnets.

Operational handoff items (draft):
- Confirm SIEM collectors and endpoints (syslog/HTTPS) and test retention policy.
- KMS/HSM integration: provide key policy and rotation window (we recommend 90 days).
- Runbook: steps to failover edge relay to secondary region and rollback model-serving routing.

See attached controlplane-dataflow-v2.svg for an annotated lane diagram. I’ll be at the Tue 09:00 PT slot; we should lock in the runbook owners in the call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: controlplane-dataflow-v2.svg (SVG, 1 file)

Subject: Re: Atlas Health VPC requirements + initial topology (for review)

Thanks Karthik — this is great. A few clarifications inline:

- Edge relay: data-plane only (we will not host control endpoints there).
- Egress model: we prefer a stateful proxy cluster (squid/Envoy) in the shared services subnet — this gives us observability and policy enforcement.
- SIEM: collectors will be at 10.5.10.12:514 (syslog) and HTTPS endpoint for telemetry ingestion at https://siem.atlashealth.internal/ingest.
- KMS: we use a cloud HSM appliance; key ARNs will be provided during the call. Rotation: 60 days preferred.

I’ve uploaded an exported archive with our networking artefacts: atlas-networking-export.zip. Also included a CSV with NAT/firewall ACLs.

Looking forward to Tue.

—Alex
Alex Romero

Atlas Health Systems

- Edge relay remains data-plane only; we recommend mTLS tunnel for callback paths into the control VPC.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood will support HSM-backed key stores. Kimberly, please follow up on policy mapping and rotation cadence (Alex requested 60 days).
